Let’s dive into Chapter 7—The Art of Asking Questions: Guiding Your Reading Journey.
Have you ever noticed how the quality of your questions can completely change the way you understand something? Whether you’re just starting a book or digging deep into its pages, the questions you ask act like a flashlight—illuminating corners you might have missed, clearing up confusion, and opening new doors to explore.
There are four essential questions you’ll want to keep in mind whenever you pick up a new book.
First, ask yourself, What’s this book about as a whole? In other words, what’s the big idea here? What’s the main subject, the purpose, and how wide does the author cast their net?
Next, dig a little deeper: What’s being said in detail, and how? Here, you’re looking for the key arguments, the evidence, and the structure behind the author’s reasoning.
Then comes a critical step: Is the book true, in whole or in part? Does the author’s argument really hold up? Are the claims backed by solid evidence, or do they fall apart under closer inspection?
And finally, ask yourself, What of it? Why does this book matter? How does it connect to what you already know, and what does it mean for how you think or what you do next?
You don’t have to answer all these questions at once. Think of them as your guide at every stage of reading. For example, during that first, quick look—what we call inspectional reading—you’ll probably focus on the big picture. When you get into analytical reading, you’ll want to break down the details and test the arguments. And if you’re comparing ideas across several books—what’s known as syntopical reading—you’ll start to see how different authors answer these same questions in their own ways.
Remember, asking questions isn’t a sign that you’re lost or confused—it’s actually a sign that you’re engaged and curious. It keeps your mind sharp and your eyes open for discovery.
Over time, you’ll develop your own set of questions that fit your interests and help you read with a deeper sense of purpose.
So, next time you open a book, don’t be afraid to shine your flashlight into those hidden corners—your questions might just lead you somewhere surprising.
